first: Bring your raingear, fall salmon fishing is fair on Nehalem, Tillamook, and Nestucca bays. All basins are still producing Chinook and coho salmon. The North Coast rivers finally got some rain which will move some fish up into the rivers and may slow fishing in the bay, but there are still fresh fish coming through. Wild coho retention is now closed on these basins, no wild coho adults may be retained as of Oct. 28. Angling for hatchery coho is still open and there are hatchery coho coming through Tillamook and Nehalem bays. See the regulation updates online at Fall Coastal Salmon Management for details on seasons and bag limits.

North Coast Rivers finally got some rain, and although the rivers only came up a little it was enough to move some fish in. Fall Chinook were reported moving into the lower river and fishing picked up at the hatchery hole. Fall Chinook should be moving into the lower reaches of the Necanicum, Nehalem, Kilchis, Wilson, and Nestucca Rivers as well.
The Trask River, North Fork Nehalem River, and Lower Columbia Tributaries should have hatchery coho arriving with the recent rains.
Try some late season trout fishing on either Garrison or Floras Lakes. Garrison Lake in particular usually has some fairly good numbers of trout that carry over from the spring stockings.
Anglers are still picking up fall chinook trolling the Chetco River estuary.
Empire, Saunders, and Butterfield Lakes were stocked recently with legal trout.

Coho salmon are moving into the lower parts of the North Santiam. Spinners such as Blue Fox are usually effective but bobbers and eggs will work as well. Best sections currently are from Green's Bridge down to Jefferson, as well as further down into the mainstem of the Santiam River.

Walleye fishing has been good along stretches of the Willamette River from Peoria downstream to Independence. A jet boat is the best option for getting at fish on some stretches, but fishing in 12-18 feet of water, especially trolling a worm spinner downstream a little faster than the currant has been netting some good-sized walleye.
Following trophy trout stockings, the Fall River has been fishing exceptionally well.
Pine Nursery Pond in Bend was recently stocked with rainbow and brown trout.
Reports of consistent trout fishing on the lower Deschutes around the Trout Creek area.

Tiger Muskies are hungry and aggressive at Phillips Reservoir. Try your luck before winter sets in. Water temperature is prime right now in the low 50°F. Fishing should remain hot until water temps drop below 45°F. As an added bonus, the low water levels will concentrate fish and may make catching fish easier.
Coho fishing has been great on the lower Umatilla River. Expect fishing to remain good into November. Summer steelhead are also present and will become more prominent as the season progresses.
Anglers are catching steelhead in both the Grande Ronde and Imnaha Rivers. Focus lower on both rivers this time of year.
Fishing for trout at Lost Creek Reservoir.

Malheur Reservoir – great for Rainbow Trout from 10-22". Common sizes are 12-16" but we captured fish up to 22" in our sampling this week. We also fly-fished it in the evening and morning and had catches of 10+ trout/hr. We saw people having success trolling and bank fishing with bait as well. Water temperatures were in the mid 50's. You can launch a boat from the boat ramp. Water is up to the old school bus. If you know you know.

Yellowjacket Reservoir – Great fishing without a crowd! We sampled last week and found fish from 8-18" with a common size of 12-15". We fished leech patterns under an indicator mid-day and had non-stop action. Water temperatures are in the mid-50's here, too.
Current and upcoming fishing opportunities:
Angling for coho has been winding down, but some anglers have still been catching around the Longview area as well as near the mouth of the Sandy River.
Bonneville Dam to McNary Dam: Weekly checking showed 22 walleye kept, and 20 walleye released for 13 boats (27 anglers).
Marine fishing. As of Jan 1, 2026, an Ocean Endorsement is needed for most recreational anglers fishing in the ocean. Check the Ocean Endorsement page for more information.
Marine fishing. Report unusual fish and ocean conditions

Marine fishing. Have you encountered unusual fish or ocean conditions off the Oregon Coast this year? With warm El Niño waters pushing up the coast, we're starting to see unusual tropical visitors migrating north! Report your on-the-water observations to CaCurrent.Observations@noaa.gov (more information available here ). Your observations are critical to understanding how changing ocean conditions affect what we see offshore.

mymapsSample.name: Alton Baker Canal
mymapsSample.about:
Alton Baker Pond and Canoe Canal are located within Alton Baker Park, one of the most popular and multi-functional parks in Eugene.
The park is located on the north bank of the Willamette River just east of the Ferry Street Bridge and Coburg Road. It is accessible by foot or bike from either side of the river via the River Bank Trails. By car you can enter via the Club Road underpass off Coburg Road or from Autzen Stadium off MLK/Centennial.
Located with in the park are two ponds and a canal, which can be accessed by rented canoes during the summer months.

mymapsSample.name: Benson Lake
mymapsSample.about:
This is a 40-acre lake located in Benson State Park in the Columbia River Gorge. From Portland, head east on I-84, park is located on the south side of the freeway approx. 1/2 mile west of Multnomah Falls.
Fish species: rainbow trout, white crappie, largemouth bass, brown bullhead
Benson State Recreation Area (http://www.oregonstateparks.org/park_147.php)

mymapsSample.name: Bethany Pond
mymapsSample.about:
This is a 10-acre pond located at Bethany west of Portland. The pond is maintained by Tualatin Hills Park and Rec. (http://www.thprd.org/parks/parkdetail.cfm?id=23) Amenities include picnic tables, restrooms, and a paved, ADA accessible trail.
Fish species: rainbow trout, largemouth bass, crappie, bluegill, bullhead

mymapsSample.name: Big Creek Reservoir #1
mymapsSample.about:
This is a 20-acre reservoir on Big Creek Road northeast of Newport, offering year-round fishing.
Fish species: rainbow trout, bass, brown bullhead
